_notes.homebrew_empty: Chapters marked homebrew: true with empty fields are custom chapters awaiting lore input from the community.
_notes.strengths_weaknesses: These axes are used to weight cascade menu options and stratagem pool composition. Strengths elevate matching options; weaknesses depress them.
_notes.faction_affinity: Which enemy type this chapter's doctrine is historically optimized against. Affects cascade menu weighting when that faction is present on the committed planet.
_notes.execution_style: One-phrase summary used to shape Champion option weighting in the cascade.
_notes.black_shield_note: Black Shield has no chapter affinity by definition — they are warriors who have renounced their chapter. Neutral on all axes, no bonuses or penalties.

chapters.name: Angels of Defiance
chapters.lore_summary: A Primaris-only Dark Angels successor raised during the Ultima Founding, embodying their primarch's legendary tenacity and his Legion's ability to bear great suffering to achieve victory. Organised in the Unforgiven pattern with Inner Circle and Deathwing and Ravenwing equivalents, they carry the shame of the Fallen alongside all their brothers. They earned commendations during the Indomitus Crusade and deployed to the Nachmund Rift War against Chaos forces threatening the vital Nachmund Gauntlet. Their defining trait is unyielding endurance that refuses to break under any pressure.

chapters.name: Angels Encarmine
chapters.lore_summary: A relentlessly active Blood Angels successor of the Sanguinary Brotherhood, the Angels Encarmine are famed for continual campaigning, severe attrition, and a large Death Company that reflects the strain of their gene-seed flaw. They are aloof and disdainful of weakness, but they answer every Imperial call for aid and fight with fierce, zealous courage. Their red-and-black heraldry reflects a chapter that has turned constant war into doctrine, paying for every victory in blood.

chapters.name: Angels of Vengeance
chapters.lore_summary: A grim, dour Unforgiven Chapter descended from the Dark Angels, retaining jet-black armour and the secret of the Fallen. They fight with stubborn, relentless frontal assaults, refusing to retreat even against overwhelming odds, which has repeatedly brought them near destruction. Historically deployed against Chaos Space Marines and traitors, whom they hunt with single-minded zeal alongside their pursuit of the Fallen. Their defining flaw is an inflexible refusal to withdraw that costs them horrific casualties.

chapters.name: Black Shield
chapters.lore_summary: Warriors who have renounced their chapter identity entirely, bearing black shields with no heraldry. They bring no chapter doctrine, no affinity, no bias — only the Long Watch. In the cascade they contribute no weighting in either direction.

chapters.name: Black Templars
chapters.lore_summary: A fanatically zealous Imperial Fists successor organised as a perpetual Crusade rather than a Codex Chapter, eschewing Librarians out of hatred of the psychic. They specialise in overwhelming close-assault charges driven by faith, closing to melee as fast as possible. Historically deployed against Chaos, heretics and xenos across endless crusades, they purge any taint of the witch. Their flaw is reckless zealotry and distrust of psykers that can blind them tactically.

chapters.name: Bleeding Hearts
chapters.lore_summary: A Blood Angels successor chapter who have forged a hunter-martyr culture around their proximity to the Black Rage. They do not suppress or mourn the Sanguinary curse but treat it as a sacred burden worn like a trophy — the Rage walks close, yet discipline over annihilation defines them. They hunt xenos relentlessly, adorning their wargear with the fangs and trophies of slain enemies, and regard self-sacrifice in the Emperor's name as the highest honour. Brothers who ultimately fall to the Rage are venerated rather than shamed, their sacrifice consecrating the chapter's ongoing hunt.

chapters.name: Blood Angels
chapters.lore_summary: A noble First Founding-descended Chapter renowned for artistry, aerial assault and elite close-combat prowess. They favour fast jump-pack strikes and ferocious melee, blending savagery with refinement. Deployed across all theatres against Chaos, xenos including Tyranids at the Devastation of Baal, and heretics. Their curse is the Red Thirst and the Black Rage, which can drive battle-brothers into uncontrollable bloodlust and madness.

chapters.name: Blood Ravens
chapters.lore_summary: A secretive Codex-compliant Chapter whose Founding, gene-seed and primarch are genuinely unknown, their records beginning only in M37. They field an unusually high proportion of Librarians, who command units and guide the Chapter with battlefield foresight. Deployed broadly against Chaos warbands, Eldar and Orks rather than one signature foe. Their defining trait is an obsessive hunger for lost knowledge and the unsettling mystery of their own dark origins.

chapters.name: Brazen Minotaurs
chapters.lore_summary: A Codex-compliant Chapter from the jungle world Tauron, renowned for blunt, direct warfare and a desire to utterly eradicate rather than merely defeat foes. They favour brutal hand-to-hand combat and frontal charges, used as a blunt instrument of force. Historically deployed against Orks of WAAAGH! Grakka and Nurgle-aligned Chaos warbands such as Empyrion's Blight, often alongside the Raven Guard. Their flaw is overextension and heavy losses from their headlong aggression.

chapters.name: Carcharodons
chapters.lore_summary: A nomadic, fleet-based Chapter known as the Space Sharks, suspected Raven Guard successors who roam the outer void serving the 'Void Father'. They fight in eerie silence using speed, stealth ambushes, swift withdrawals and absolute close-quarters brutality. Deployed as ruthless enforcers against traitors and rebels, notably during the Badab War. Their flaw is a savage, predatory ruthlessness and reliance on aging, heavily modified wargear.

chapters.name: Carmine Blades
chapters.lore_summary: A Blood Angels successor from the feral world Haldroth, long mistaken for Ultramarines descendants until Astorath revealed their true lineage in late M41. They are savage but insular warriors who fight with ferocious close assault and Reiver shadow-war tactics. Deployed against Chaos such as the Black Legion and Tyranids at the Devastation of Baal, where they lost their Chapter Master and most of their strength. Their flaw is the Red Thirst and Black Rage they long concealed.

chapters.name: Celestial Lions
chapters.lore_summary: A disciplined, honourable Imperial Fists successor from Elysium IX, using distinctive ranks such as Pride Leader and prizing storytelling and brotherhood. They fight as steadfast sons of Dorn with fast flanking maneuvers and proud line warfare. Famed for opposing the Inquisition after the Khattar atrocity, they were reduced to fewer than a company by Orks on Armageddon amid Inquisitorial sabotage. Their tragic flaw is the dwindling, near-extinct numbers and the enmity of the Imperium's own Inquisition.

chapters.name: Cowled Wardens
chapters.lore_summary: A Dark Angels Unforgiven successor fleet-based in hollowed-out asteroids of the Sirikoid Belt, nominally tasked with purging the savage Jehangir xenos but secretly hunting a large network of the Fallen believed to operate in the region. Captured Fallen are consigned to icy catacombs carved within a nameless asteroid. Lion El'Jonson himself visited them after his awakening and led the Chapter to final victory over the Jehangir species. They joined three-quarters of the Unforgiven in the Battle of Idolatros hunting the Greater Daemon Vashtorr during the Arks of Omen campaign.

chapters.name: Crimson Fists
chapters.lore_summary: A stoic Imperial Fists successor reduced to just 16 survivors when a faltering planetary-defence missile detonated their arsenal on Rynn's World, devastating the Chapter. They are masters of siege warfare, marksmanship and grim last-stand defence, fighting with disciplined resilience against impossible odds. Historically deployed against Orks and Chaos across the Loki Sector. Their defining trait is dogged endurance born of near-extinction and Dorn's stubborn refusal to yield.

chapters.name: Dark Angels
chapters.lore_summary: The secretive First Legion and leaders of the Unforgiven, organised around the Inner Circle, Deathwing and Ravenwing. They employ versatile combined-arms doctrine, from Terminator strikes to fast bike assaults, with grim discipline. Deployed across all fronts but obsessively hunting the Fallen traitors of their own bloodline against Chaos. Their flaw is the corrosive secrecy and shame of the Fallen that drives them to dangerous ends.

chapters.name: Dark Krakens
chapters.lore_summary: A Salamanders successor raised from Greyshields and based on the ocean world Naktis, where the native population hunts bioluminescent megafauna for sport and survival. Echoing this culture, the Dark Krakens seek out the largest and most numerous foes, fighting with all the resilience and stubbornness of their gene-sire Vulkan. Deployed against Hive Fleet Leviathan in the Pankallis Sub-sector's Cordon Impenetra, they fought gruelling months-long campaigns in alien forests with patient skirmish tactics and steadfast refusal to yield. Battle-brothers adorn their armour with bioluminescent symbols and ocean-beast trophies as campaign markings.

chapters.name: Death Exorcists
chapters.lore_summary: A Blood Angels successor chapter who have rejected the Sanguinary curse as a sacred gift, naming it instead "Horus's plague" — a corruption to be actively purged. They cultivate an unusually strong psyker tradition and rigorous mental discipline to resist the Red Thirst and Black Rage on their own terms rather than endure it. Their combat doctrine favours brutal shock assault followed by scorched-earth denial of the battlefield, ensuring no enemy and no taint remains. Brothers who resist the Rage without succumbing are honoured as proof that the plague can be exorcised by will and psychic clarity alone.
chapters.execution_style: psychic shock assault with scorched-earth follow-through

chapters.name: Death Spectres
chapters.lore_summary: A Raven Guard successor of the mysterious 13th Founding, garrisoned on the cemetery world Occludus to guard the galaxy against the horrors of the Ghoul Stars. They favour stealth, infiltration and guerrilla tactics, and venerate death, requiring aspirants to return from near-death by will alone. Deployed against Necron Flayed Ones, Cythor Fiends and other deathless xenos, plus Chaos during the 13th Black Crusade. Their gene-seed quirk causes albinism, and their Chapter Master slowly dies upon the psychic Throne of Glass.

chapters.name: Dragonspears
chapters.lore_summary: A fleet-based Salamanders successor renowned as expert Greenskin hunters, winning renown alongside the Space Wolves against Orks at the Gnarion Reef. Their culture of self-sacrifice and endocannibalism — using their Omophagea implants to consume a portion of fallen brothers and preserve their memories — embodies Vulkan's creed that no brother is ever truly lost. They deployed eight companies in the Prosperan Rift War against the Thousand Sons and later honoured ancient oaths of brotherhood to join the Space Wolves against Ghazghkull Thraka's Great WAAAGH!. Their constant fleet movement made contact with the Salamanders difficult for many years.

chapters.name: Epsilon Paladins
chapters.lore_summary: Fleet-based Imperial Fists successors founded in the Era Indomitus under Chapter Master Dekra Akalius, bearing silver armour with a golden left arm. They roam the galaxy seeking faltering Imperial bastions and those in desperate need, mastering both defensive siege warfare and proactive honour charges. Active in Segmentum Pacificus and deployed to the Recidious System during the Fourth Tyrannic War alongside their progenitor chapter. Their warcry is 'For Honour! For Duty! For Dorn!'

chapters.name: Exorcists
chapters.lore_summary: A highly controversial Imperial Fists successor created under Inquisitorial seal to combat daemons, whose aspirants must survive ritual daemonic possession and exorcism. Codex-compliant but organised into twelve companies, they are exceptional daemon-hunters resistant to Chaos corruption. Historically deployed against the daemons and forces of Chaos, fighting them on par with the Grey Knights. Their flaw is the heretical taint of their initiation, which would see them purged if widely known.

chapters.name: Flesh Tearers
chapters.lore_summary: A savage Blood Angels successor led by Chapter Master Gabriel Seth, defined by an abnormally severe susceptibility to the Red Thirst and Black Rage. They strike first and alone with frenzied, blood-soaked close-assault savagery, distrusted by allies for their loss of control. Historically deployed against Tyranids at the Devastation of Baal and Chaos traitors, nearly excommunicated after atrocities on Armageddon. Their flaw is the genetic curse that has driven them to the brink of extinction.

chapters.name: Genesis Chapter
chapters.lore_summary: The first of the Ultramarines' Primogenitor successors, dogmatically loyal to Guilliman and the Codex Astartes from their homeworld Newfound. They fight as model Codex Marines with balanced, disciplined combined-arms doctrine, often filling gaps in Ultramarine companies. Deployed broadly against Orks, Chaos and Tyranids including Exterminatus missions ahead of Hive Fleet Leviathan. Their defining trait is rigid Codex orthodoxy and unwavering devotion to their primarch.

chapters.name: Hawk Lords
chapters.lore_summary: A Codex Chapter from Preyspire suspected to descend from the Ultramarines Legion's 21st Chapter, 'The Hawks', renowned for the skill of their pilots. They eschew drop pods in favour of Thunderhawk and Stormtalon air insertion, mastering low-altitude aerial assault and rapid strikes. Deployed against Orks during the War of the Beast, Chaos at Cadia, and unknown xenos near their homeworld. Their conflicting recorded lineage and reliance on air power are their notable traits.

chapters.name: Hospitallers
chapters.lore_summary: A fleet-based Imperial Fists successor famous for rejecting the Codex Astartes, organising into only three companies built around sacred vows: defeating the Emperor's foes, protecting His faithful, and eternal vigilance. Uniquely among Space Marines, they recognise the Emperor as a literal god and maintain close ties with the Adeptus Ministorum, serving as itinerant crusaders guarding Imperial trade and pilgrimage routes. Their secretive veteran elite 'The Vigil' operates outside the three-company structure. They harbour bitter enmity toward the Iron Hands after Clan Raukaan boarded their flagship and abducted their Venerable Dreadnought Augustine Galvarro.
strengths: protection of Imperial routes and faithful

chapters.name: Imperial Fists
chapters.lore_summary: The stalwart sons of Rogal Dorn, the Imperium's foremost masters of siege warfare and fortification, defenders of the Emperor's Palace during the Heresy. They excel at defensive lines, marksmanship and breaking or holding fortresses with iron discipline. Deployed across all theatres against Chaos, Orks and rebels, ever bearing Dorn's legacy. Their flaw is an obsessive sense of duty and self-flagellating guilt, and a stubbornness in the face of stronger foes.

chapters.name: Imperius Reavers
chapters.lore_summary: An Ultramarines successor holding dominion over the turbulent Vidar Sector on the Eastern Fringe, a volatile region plagued by alien threats, daemon incursions and corrupt noble families. Veterans of the First Tyrannic War, their 2nd Company 'The Stormbringers' are renowned experts at detecting and eradicating Genestealer hybrid cults. They cleansed their own homeworld Praedis Zeta of a Genestealer Magus's corruption in 645.M39, showcasing their defining role as relentless hunters of xenos infiltration. They serve as a steadfast bulwark against the twin threats of the alien and the daemon at the galaxy's far eastern edge.
weaknesses: isolated far from the core Imperium
volatile corrupt political environment in their sector

chapters.name: Iron Hands
chapters.lore_summary: The cold, logical sons of Ferrus Manus, who abhor the weakness of flesh and replace their bodies with cybernetic augmetics. They wage methodical attrition warfare with heavy firepower, armour and unmatched mechanised resilience. Deployed broadly against Chaos, Orks and xenos, harbouring grudges since the betrayal at Isstvan V. Their flaw is an emotionless contempt for weakness and over-reliance on technology that can blind them.

chapters.name: Iron Hounds
chapters.lore_summary: An Ultramarines successor from Orinus in the Ultima Segmentum, renowned for relentless pursuit that continues until every last foe is slain. Steadfast allies of the Ultramarines, they pledged warriors to the defence of Ultramar in the Plague Wars against the Death Guard and at the Third War for Damnos against the Szarekhan Dynasty Necrons. They subsequently joined the assault on the Scourge Stars to take the fight to Nurgle's daemon-held worlds, and Imperial high command believes the entire Chapter may have been destroyed there. Their defining trait is an iron refusal to abandon the hunt regardless of cost.
weaknesses: may be destroyed fighting in the Scourge Stars

chapters.name: Iron Lords
chapters.lore_summary: A Codex-compliant Iron Hands successor noted for stern demeanour and uncompromising hatred of all xenos life, maintaining the blockade of the Grendl Stars since M38. They fight with disciplined firepower and cybernetic resilience to confine the hyper-violent Barghesi and battle encroaching threats. Historically deployed against the Barghesi, Tyranids of Hive Fleet Kraken and the T'au. Their flaw is isolation in Imperium Nihilus, cut off from reinforcement amid endless desperate battles.

chapters.name: Iron Ravens
chapters.lore_summary: A Raven Guard Primaris successor specialising in sudden decisive drop assaults called 'the Blade of Corax', where 10th Company scouts spend months building intelligence so the main force strikes with overwhelming and unstoppable precision. Unlike more rigidly stealth-focused Raven Guard successors, they are tactically flexible, shaped by their Greyshield experience fighting alongside warriors of many gene-lines during the Indomitus Crusade. They are not solely committed to stealth, adapting their doctrine to whatever enemy and theatre they face. They bear their iron resolve as their defining Chapter identity.
weaknesses: months of preparation required before striking

chapters.name: Knights of the Raven
chapters.lore_summary: A secretive Codex-compliant Raven Guard successor from the feudal world Coralax, so reclusive that even the Deathwatch and Inquisition know little of them. They wage stealthy hit-and-run guerrilla warfare using the Raven Guard ambush doctrine and a cryptic battle-tongue. As penance for shedding fellow Astartes' blood, they now fight a guerrilla war against splinters of Hive Fleet Kraken. Their flaw is extreme secrecy and isolation from the wider Imperium.

chapters.name: Lamenters
chapters.lore_summary: A tragic Blood Angels successor of the Cursed Founding, dogged by relentless misfortune despite their heroic compassion. A flexible, self-reliant fleet-based Chapter, they fight pragmatically and adapt to scarce resources after fighting without Imperial support. They sided mistakenly with the rebels in the Badab War, then were reduced to barely three companies battling Tyranids of Hive Fleet Kraken on their penitent crusade. Their flaw is supernatural ill-fortune and the eventual return of the Black Rage.

chapters.name: Marines Errant
chapters.lore_summary: A fleet-based Ultramarines-lineage Chapter, credited as a successor of the Eagle Warriors, whose battle-brothers crusade independently across the galaxy. They follow a Codex doctrine modified for autonomous fleet operations, with captains commanding individual vessels for years at a time. Deployed in the Corinth Crusade against Orks and the Badab War, where they were ambushed and badly mauled by the Mantis Warriors. Their flaw is the heavy losses and command decapitation suffered at Bellerophon's Fall and Vilamus.

chapters.name: Marines Malevolent
chapters.lore_summary: A Loyalist Chapter of unknown genetic origin founded in the 32nd Millennium, the Marines Malevolent are deeply committed to the destruction of the Imperium's enemies but are infamous for callous disregard for civilian life and excessive collateral damage. Adhering to anti-psyker Council of Nikaea tenets, they pursue victory by any means necessary, believing innocence does not exist—only degrees of guilt. Notorious for shelling a refugee camp on Armageddon to kill an Ork warband, and for attempted salvage of Adeptus Mechanicus wargear from the Forge Ship Archimedes Rex, they have clashed repeatedly with the Salamanders and drawn repeated Inquisitorial censure. Their battle record is exemplary; their methods are not.
weaknesses: isolated from allies by brutal methods

chapters.name: Mantis Warriors
chapters.lore_summary: A loyalist White Scars successor renowned for guerrilla warfare, devastating ambushes, and sudden large-scale assaults. Guardians of the Endymion Cluster for millennia, the Mantis Warriors were deceived by the Astral Claws into joining the Badab War secession. Absolved of treachery, they were sentenced to a 100-year penitent crusade, forbidden to recruit. Now critically understrength, they fight with a deep streak of shame and an unbreakable need for redemption, deploying hit-and-run tactics honed across centuries of isolation.

chapters.name: Mentors
chapters.lore_summary: A cerebral Ultramarines successor and former 'Mentor Legion' that acts as a test-bed for experimental Imperial military technology from a secret fortress-monastery. They loan elite squads to other Imperial forces, serving as special-operations troops and force-multiplying unit leaders much like the Deathwatch. Deployed in highly specialised missions across the galaxy against varied foes, valuing knowledge and adaptability above all. Their trait is extreme secrecy and an extraordinary capacity for learning the art of war.

chapters.name: Minotaurs
chapters.lore_summary: A brutal, secretive Chapter acting as the enforcers of the High Lords of Terra, specialising in fighting other Space Marines. Led by Asterion Moloc, they combine masterful siegecraft and logistics with savage melee and overwhelming weight of numbers and rare wargear. Notoriously deployed during the Badab War to ambush the Lamenters and force their surrender, and against the Necrons in the Orphean War. Their flaw is a paranoid, bloody-handed ruthlessness and pragmatism that borders on the dishonourable.

chapters.name: Necropolis Hawks
chapters.lore_summary: A Raven Guard Primaris successor extensively trained in close-quarters urban warfare, veterans of a dozen brutal city-fights. Their pragmatic brutality and relentlessly measured aggression turned the tide on Vigilus during the War of Beasts, taking the Dontoria hivesprawl building by building and ruthlessly demolishing zones deemed lost. They deployed to the Fourth Tyrannic War to defend the Segmentum Pacificus from Hive Fleet Leviathan and fought in the Nachmund Rift War. Battle-brothers bear their tactical insignia on their backpacks so comrades can identify them even through the choking smoke and dust of urban war.
weaknesses: Drukhari captured several battle-brothers on Vigilus

chapters.name: Revilers
chapters.lore_summary: A grim and austere chapter with a fearsome reputation for pitiless, terror-forward prosecution of war. Their iconography and battlefield conduct project intimidation as a deliberate weapon, combining psychological pressure with hard attritional violence to break hostile morale before the final breach. They are known for strict operational discipline and a culture that prizes function over ceremony, enduring long campaigns by accepting hardship as routine. Their flaws are an inflexible severity and a tendency toward methods other Imperial allies can find difficult to stomach.
weaknesses: strained interoperability with less austere allies

chapters.name: Raptors
chapters.lore_summary: A Raven Guard successor led by Chapter Master Lias Issodon, famed for exceptional survival, marksmanship and adaptation after being driven near extinction multiple times. They are masters of guerrilla warfare, infiltration, sabotage and precision strikes on enemy command and supply. Deployed in the Badab War, the Taros Campaign against the T'au, and across the Indomitus Crusade against Chaos and xenos. Their flaw is chronic understrength from operating as independent companies.

chapters.name: Raven Guard
chapters.lore_summary: The First Founding masters of stealth and lightning warfare, scions of Corvus Corax, who strike fast and lethal from the shadows. They specialise in infiltration, ambush, assassination and precise overwhelming assaults, disdaining reckless frontal charges and heavy armour. Deployed against Chaos, Orks and the T'au on the Eastern Fringe, ever mourning their losses at the Drop Site Massacre. Their flaw is depleted, deteriorating gene-seed and chronically low numbers.

chapters.name: Red Scorpions
chapters.lore_summary: A fleet-based Chapter of fanatical Imperial purists obsessed with the purity of their gene-seed and the divinity of the Emperor, venerating no single primarch. They are rigid Codex literalists who fight with disciplined Tactical-heavy formations and refuse to serve alongside abhumans or 'tainted' Chapters. Deployed at the Siege of Vraks against Chaos and daemons, against Tyranids on Beta Anphelion IV, and in the Badab War. Their flaw is isolationist purity that makes them distrustful and inflexible.

chapters.name: Red Templars
chapters.lore_summary: A Codex-compliant Imperial Fists successor of unknown founding, experts in search-and-destroy and relentless pursuit operations. Directly tasked by the High Lords of Terra alongside the Minotaurs to hunt down and destroy the excommunicated Night Reapers Chapter, they served as the persistent hounds pursuing their quarry across a dozen star systems over three years of running battles while the Minotaurs delivered the killing blow at Perun Cross. They make distinctive use of Assault Bikes at the squad level, underscoring their identity as mobile hunters. Their defining trait is the grim, relentless expertise of a Chapter built to run down the condemned.

chapters.name: Salamanders
chapters.lore_summary: The resilient, humane sons of Vulkan from the death world Nocturne, master artificers who prize self-sacrifice and protecting innocents. They favour flame and melta weapons, master-crafted wargear and close-range firefights, fighting with stoic endurance. Deployed broadly against Chaos, Orks and xenos, notably in the Badab War. Their notable traits are their onyx-black skin and burning red eyes, deep humanity, and relatively small numbers from slow Nocturnean recruitment.

chapters.name: Scythes of the Emperor
chapters.lore_summary: An Ultramarines successor from Sotha, descended from veterans who guarded the Pharos, whose homeworld was devoured by Hive Fleet Kraken. Reduced to barely a company, they wage a vengeful war against the Tyranids using hit-and-run tactics and boarding 'Saviour Squads' to recover battle-brothers and wargear from hive ships. Defined by their near-annihilation at the Giant's Coffin on Miral and rebuilding via Primaris reinforcements. Their flaw is catastrophic understrength and the trauma of genestealer infiltration.

chapters.name: Sons of Medusa
chapters.lore_summary: An Iron Hands successor born from the Moirae Schism exiles, organised into War Clans and ratified as a Chapter by Imperial edict in 011.M37. Like their forebears they abhor weak flesh and rely on cybernetics, favouring aggressive armoured spearheads and mechanised assault. Deployed in the Badab War, the Great Cull and against Chaos at Mordian, and notorious for seizing wargear from foes. Their flaw is a reputation as scavenging 'carrion crows' and lingering distrust from their schismatic origins.

chapters.name: Space Wolves
chapters.lore_summary: The fierce, independent sons of Leman Russ from Fenris, organised into Great Companies and defiant of the Codex Astartes. They fight with savage pack-hunting close assault, terror tactics and ferocious melee, blending Fenrisian barbarism with cunning. Deployed across all theatres against Chaos, Orks and traitors as the Emperor's executioners. Their flaw is the genetic Curse of the Wolfen and the Canis Helix that can turn battle-brothers into beasts, and their disdain for outside authority.

chapters.name: Storm Giants
chapters.lore_summary: A Codex-compliant Chapter of unknown origins created in the 36th Millennium or earlier, widely suspected to be Salamanders successors due to their similar physique, markings and tactical preference for close-range firefights. They display heightened physical strength even for Space Marines, possibly due to a mutation in their Biscopea gene-seed organ, though the Chapter has refused every Magi-genetor request to study them. They sent five companies to the Third War for Armageddon and fought alongside the Black Templars purging Chaos cultists during the Second Purging of Lastrati. Their four-stage Vindicator-supported assault doctrine is a signature of their close-range firepower approach.

chapters.name: Tempestuous Angels
chapters.lore_summary: A Salamanders successor chapter known informally as the "Emperor's Altruists," who hold the protection of the defenceless as their highest calling above all tactical considerations. Their history is bound to the tragedy of Drossmire, a world lost to fire — an event that shapes their doctrine and their grief in equal measure. They combine Vulkan's selfless creed with a storm-and-shield iconography, casting themselves as the wall between the innocent and the tempest. Self-sacrifice in defence of others is not merely expected but celebrated, and they field a disproportionate number of warriors trained in protective close-assault.

chapters.name: The Drakes
chapters.lore_summary: A Salamanders successor chapter whose culture is built entirely around fire as both purification and weapon. They hold that fire reveals what must be preserved and destroys what must not be, and their initiation rites involve sustained exposure to intense heat as proof of the drake's temper within. Their name invokes the primordial drake — older and more primal than the dragon — and they employ overwhelming incendiary assault as both tactical doctrine and spiritual act. They are fiercely protective of their battle-brothers in the way a drake guards its brood, binding themselves to those they fight beside through fire-forged oaths.
weaknesses: limited tactical flexibility outside incendiary doctrine

chapters.name: Tigers Argent
chapters.lore_summary: A Loyalist Codex-compliant chapter of uncertain origin associated with the Calixis Sector since the Angevin Crusade in early M39. Their homeworld, Icefang, sits in a perilous region close to both the Great Rift and Pariah Nexus, forcing the chapter into repeated defensive campaigns against multiple threats. Despite sustained attrition, their strike forces are noted for refusing defeat and repeatedly restoring the line after successive incursions. Icefang has become a regional sanctuary, and the chapter's doctrine reflects grim endurance under constant pressure rather than pursuit of singular glory.

chapters.name: Tome Keepers
chapters.lore_summary: An Ultramarines successor from the irradiated Desert World Istrouma in Segmentum Pacificus, founded after the War of the Beast. They are warriors and scholars equally, keeping meticulous records of every battle and foe, driven by the short-lived culture of their homeworld where everything must be chronicled against the certainty of early death. They favour clinical battlefield discipline and deep knowledge of their enemies over brute aggression, and field an unusually high number of Librarians. They waged a 200-year war against the Necron Thokt Dynasty before participating in the Argovon Campaign of the Pariah Crusade, but their unfiltered record-keeping has earned them the enmity of the Ecclesiarchy.

chapters.name: Ultramarines
chapters.lore_summary: The exemplary First Founding Chapter and authors of the Codex Astartes, ruling the realm of Ultramar from Macragge as the template for all Space Marines. They embody balanced, disciplined and tactically flexible combined-arms warfare. Deployed across every front against Chaos, Orks, the T'au and Tyranids, famously halting Hive Fleet Behemoth at Macragge and the Kraken at Ichar IV. Their defining trait is unmatched discipline and the leadership of the resurrected primarch Roboute Guilliman.

chapters.name: White Templars
chapters.lore_summary: An Imperial Fists successor chapter identified by stark white-and-black heraldry and a stoic culture of duty under siege conditions. Their doctrine emphasizes disciplined line-holding, relentless counter-assaults, and endurance over theatrics, meeting prolonged pressure with stubborn cohesion rather than dramatic maneuver. They are regarded as austere, pragmatic crusaders who value oath, structure, and battlefield constancy. Their chief weakness is strategic rigidity: they excel when the line must be held, but can be slower to exploit fluid opportunities than more mobile chapters.
weaknesses: less suited to highly fluid maneuver warfare

chapters.name: White Scars
chapters.lore_summary: The swift sons of Jaghatai Khan from Chogoris, masters of lightning-fast mobile warfare and hit-and-run cavalry tactics on bikes and fast attack vehicles. They strike with sudden encircling speed and overwhelming momentum before vanishing. Deployed across all theatres against Chaos, Orks and xenos, valuing the hunt and the kill. Their trait is unrivalled mobility and a nomadic warrior culture that other Chapters find inscrutable.

chapters.name: Wolfspear
chapters.lore_summary: A Primaris-only Space Wolves successor raised in the Ultima Founding from Greyshields of Guilliman's Unnumbered Sons, blood-brothers of the sons of Russ. They wage intimidating pack-hunting warfare with stealthy killers, swift vehicles and terror tactics that sow confusion. Deployed against Chaos guarding the Pit of Raukos and across Imperium Nihilus. Their flaw is the lingering Canis Helix curse and anxiety over acceptance as true Sons of Russ.
